39:1.ar: تَنزِيلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ
39:1.en: The revelation of the Scripture is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise

39:2.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ فَٱعۡبُدِ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡلِصࣰ ا لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ
39:2.en: Lo! We have revealed the Scripture unto thee (Muhammad) with truth; so worship Allah, making religion pure for Him (only)

39:3.ar: أَلَا لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡخَالِصُۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مَا نَعۡبُدُهُمۡ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ زُلۡفَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحۡكُمُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ فِي مَا هُمۡ فِيهِ يَخۡتَلِفُونَۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي مَنۡ هُوَ كَٰذِبࣱ كَفَّارࣱ‏
39:3.en: Surely pure religion is for Allah only. And those who choose protecting friends beside Him (say): We worship them only that they may bring us near unto Allah. Lo! Allah will judge between them concerning that wherein they differ. Lo! Allah guideth not him who is a liar, an ingrate

39:4.ar: لَّوۡ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدࣰ ا لَّٱصۡطَفَىٰ مِمَّا يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥۖ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّارُ
39:4.en: If Allah had willed to choose a son, He could have chosen what He would of that which He hath created. Be He Glorified! He is Allah, the One, the Absolute

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam all the names, then showed them to the angels, saying: Inform Me of the names of these, if ye are truthful

2:32.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:32.en: They said: Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise

53:23.ar: إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّآ أَسۡمَآءࣱ سَمَّيۡتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلۡطَٰنٍۚ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهۡوَى ٱلۡأَنفُسُۖ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مِّن رَّبِّهِمُ ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ
53:23.en: They are but names which ye have named, ye and your fathers, for which Allah hath revealed no warrant. They follow but a guess and that which (they) themselves desire. And now the guidance from their Lord hath come unto them

49:13.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرࣲ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ شُعُوبࣰ ا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
49:13.en: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

33:14.ar: وَلَوۡ دُخِلَتۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنۡ أَقۡطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُئِلُواْ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةَ لَأٓتَوۡهَا وَمَا تَلَبَّثُواْ بِهَآ إِلَّا يَسِيرࣰ ا
33:14.en: If the enemy had entered from all sides and they had been exhorted to treachery, they would have committed it, and would have hesitated thereupon but little

25:32.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَوۡلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ جُمۡلَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰۚ كَذَٰلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِۦ فُؤَادَكَۖ وَرَتَّلۡنَٰهُ تَرۡتِيلࣰ ا
25:32.en: And those who disbelieve say: Why is the Qur'an not revealed unto him all at once? (It is revealed) thus that We may strengthen thy heart therewith; and We have arranged it in right order

21:23.ar: لَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفۡعَلُ وَهُمۡ يُسۡـَٔلُونَ
21:23.en: He will not be questioned as to that which He doeth, but they will be questioned

3:160.ar: إِن يَنصُرۡكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمۡۖ وَإِن يَخۡذُلۡكُمۡ فَمَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَنصُرُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦۗ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
3:160.en: If Allah is your helper none can overcome you, and if He withdraw His help from you, who is there who can help you after Him? In Allah let believers put their trust

38:25.ar: فَغَفَرۡنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَۖ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلۡفَىٰ وَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:25.en: So We forgave him that; and lo! he had access to Our presence and a happy journey's end

6:59.ar: ۞وَعِندَهُۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَا يَعۡلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِۚ وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةࣲ فِي ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا رَطۡبࣲ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتَٰبࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
6:59.en: And with Him are the keys of the Invisible. None but He knoweth them. And He knoweth what is in the land and the sea. Not a leaf falleth but He knoweth it, not a grain amid the darkness of the earth, naught of wet or dry but (it is noted) in a clear record

3:26.ar: قُلِ ٱللَّهُمَّ مَٰلِكَ ٱلۡمُلۡكِ تُؤۡتِي ٱلۡمُلۡكَ مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَنزِعُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ مِمَّن تَشَآءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَن تَشَآءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَآءُۖ بِيَدِكَ ٱلۡخَيۡرُۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
3:26.en: Say: O Allah! Owner of Sovereignty! Thou givest sovereignty unto whom Thou wilt, and Thou withdrawest sovereignty from whom Thou wilt. Thou exaltest whom Thou wilt, and Thou abasest whom Thou wilt. In Thy hand is the good. Lo! Thou art Able to do all things

53:13.en: And verily he saw him yet another time

53:14.en: By the lote-tree of the utmost boundary

38:75.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓإِبۡلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسۡجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقۡتُ بِيَدَيَّۖ أَسۡتَكۡبَرۡتَ أَمۡ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡعَالِينَ
38:75.en: He said: O Iblis! What hindereth thee from falling prostrate before that which I have created with both My hands? Art thou too proud or art thou of the high exalted

6:18.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلۡقَاهِرُ فَوۡقَ عِبَادِهِۦۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
6:18.en: He is the Omnipotent over His slaves, and He is the Wise, the Knower

f1_H5rWrrC4.speaker_note: opens Az-Zumar in his weekly Arabic tafsir series after finishing Sad the week before
f1_H5rWrrC4.title: Arabic Tafsir: Opening Surat Az-Zumar (39:1-4)
f1_H5rWrrC4.one_line: After a long lesson on Iblis's arrogance, he opens Az-Zumar: obedience through sincerity, religion purely for Allah, and why intermediaries are a lie.
f1_H5rWrrC4.summary: He reviews the axis from Al-Ahzab to Az-Zumar, each surah treating a kind of obedience, then returns to Iblis from Sad: arrogance kept him from returning to the truth. Adam's worth lay in his hidden potential, shown when he learned the names. Arrogance rests on ignorance: you know your own faults for certain but not another's life or ending, and taqwa is a path walked, not something you can measure, so no comparison is valid. Humility is simply knowing yourself; racism is arrogance multiplied, and a servant with an ego is a contradiction. Az-Zumar, the summit of the axis, is the surrender of the mind, which produces sincerity, the secret of tawhid: care only for Allah's opinion, since everyone else is drowning too. The first verses stress that the Book was sent down gradually by the Mighty, whom we cannot fully grasp, and the Wise, who commands only for our benefit; worship Him with religion sincerely His, since pure religion belongs to Him alone. Those who take patrons, claiming they only bring them near, want an easier middleman; Allah calls them liars and ungrateful. Even if He had wanted a son He would have chosen something mighty, not a stone, as the Prophet saw even Jibril humbled at the Lote Tree.

outline.heading: The axis of obedience: Al-Ahzab to Az-Zumar
outline.gist: Obedience is the axis of a Muslim's life, so the Quran gives it a cluster of surahs, ending with Az-Zumar.

outline.heading: Al-Ahzab, Saba and Fatir
outline.gist: Obedience under pressure, obedience of whole societies, and obedience through knowledge, not as people imagine it.

outline.heading: Ya-Sin, As-Saffat and Sad
outline.gist: Obedience as true life, obedience when the wisdom is hidden, and obedience by returning to the truth after error.

outline.heading: Iblis: arrogance blocked his return
outline.gist: Iblis judged Adam by deeds and origin and missed the potential Allah placed in him.

outline.heading: Adam's potential: the gift of expression and learning
outline.gist: Humans can put feelings and experience into words; Adam learned and connected the names in a way the angels could not.

outline.heading: You do not know anyone's ending
outline.gist: Arrogance compares what is visible now, but no one knows how another or he himself will end.

outline.heading: Arrogance is born of ignorance
outline.gist: You know your own hand of cards but not another's; brothers fight because each thinks he knows the other.

outline.heading: You cannot even understand yourself
outline.gist: Knowing oneself is a lifelong journey; being better at engineering or medicine is not arrogance unless made into a ranking.

outline.heading: Taqwa is a path walked, not a quantity
outline.gist: One raised in evil who repented a few steps may have walked further than one raised in good; this does not change what is halal and haram.

outline.heading: No valid comparison without all the variables
outline.gist: As in a drug trial, comparison requires every variable; only Allah knows our ranks, and even a dream cannot reveal them.

outline.heading: Never say 'that could never be me'
outline.gist: Iblis sat among the angels yet fell; claiming immunity repeats his mistake, so ask Allah for safety and hold your tongue.

outline.heading: Humility is knowing yourself truly
outline.gist: I know my own faults for certain and yours only by guess; the humble man does not inflate when praised, like a balloon.

outline.heading: Humility is the master of character
outline.gist: Without humility all other virtues are worthless and no arrogant person enters Paradise; Iblis has not repented to this day.

outline.heading: Racism is collective arrogance
outline.gist: Racism is arrogance multiplied over a whole group; a servant with an ego is a useless servant.

outline.heading: Az-Zumar: the surrender of the mind
outline.gist: Earlier surahs dealt with practical obedience; this one with belief, the summit of surrender, which produces sincerity.

outline.heading: A mind that surrenders becomes sincere
outline.gist: It no longer sees any rival to Allah; Sad spoke of the sincere ones, and Allah saves those who first make their religion sincere.

outline.heading: Sincerity: a secret between the servant and his Lord
outline.gist: Care only for Allah's view of you; other people are all drowning like you, so their opinion counts for little.

outline.heading: Sincerity is the secret of tawhid
outline.gist: He is One, so your attachment should be to one; the hadith qudsi says He leaves any deed shared with a partner.

outline.heading: Verses 1-4 recited
outline.gist: Az-Zumar is clear enough to reflect on directly.

outline.heading: 'Tanzil': the Book sent down in stages
outline.gist: Gradual revelation spoke to the Prophet's circumstances and steadied his heart; a Makkan surah, probably late.

outline.heading: Al-Aziz: beyond our grasp
outline.gist: Anything whose essence we could fully understand would not be God; His names are necessary to divinity.

outline.heading: Al-Hakim, and many names at the opening
outline.gist: He commands only for our benefit; the many names here present Him so we know why He deserves sincerity.

outline.heading: Worship Him, making religion sincerely His
outline.gist: 'Din' is what you consider owed; you honour parents because He commanded it, owing nothing to anyone but Him.

outline.heading: Pure religion belongs to Allah
outline.gist: Sincerity is His right, not a favour; there is no comparison that would leave any share for others.

outline.heading: Taking patrons besides Him
outline.gist: Seeking victory from America or any army instead of Allah is taking patrons; pursue the means He set while knowing victory is His alone.

outline.heading: 'Only to bring us near': zulfa is honoured nearness
outline.gist: Each idol had a role; zulfa is the nearness of honour, unlike rulers who are near their masters only in humiliation.

outline.heading: Intermediaries like government offices
outline.gist: People want a middleman who demands little; Allah needs none, as nothing escapes His knowledge.

outline.heading: 'Allah will judge between them' and the reduction of great values
outline.gist: The phrase signals divine anger; declining civilizations shrink great values like fasting, prayer and freedom, and we must revive tawhid in full.

outline.heading: Guidance withheld from the liar and the ungrateful
outline.gist: Everyone receives guidance as direction, but only seekers receive it in the heart; 'kaffar' here means ungrateful for blessings.

outline.heading: 'Even if He had wanted a son'
outline.gist: This 'law' introduces an impossible case; even then He would have chosen a mighty creation, not a stone.

outline.heading: Jibril seen twice in his true form
outline.gist: At the first revelation Jibril filled the horizon; at the Lote Tree he was like a worn cloth before Allah's majesty.

outline.heading: The One, the Subduer
outline.gist: Everyone will worship and plead with Him in the end; our only choice is whether to do it now, with reward.

outline.heading: Outro

59:13.ar: لَأَنتُمۡ أَشَدُّ رَهۡبَةࣰ فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ لَّا يَفۡقَهُونَ
59:13.en: Ye are more awful as a fear in their bosoms than Allah. That is because they are a folk who understand not

59:14.ar: لَا يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمۡ جَمِيعًا إِلَّا فِي قُرࣰ ى مُّحَصَّنَةٍ أَوۡ مِن وَرَآءِ جُدُرِۭۚ بَأۡسُهُم بَيۡنَهُمۡ شَدِيدࣱۚ تَحۡسَبُهُمۡ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَقُلُوبُهُمۡ شَتَّىٰۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ لَّا يَعۡقِلُونَ
59:14.en: They will not fight against you in a body save in fortified villages or from behind walls. Their adversity among themselves is very great. Ye think of them as a whole whereas their hearts are divers. That is because they are a folk who have no sense

59:15.ar: كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ قَرِيبࣰ اۖ ذَاقُواْ وَبَالَ أَمۡرِهِمۡ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
59:15.en: On the likeness of those (who suffered) a short time before them, they taste the ill-effects of their own conduct, and theirs is painful punishment

59:16.ar: كَمَثَلِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ إِذۡ قَالَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ ٱكۡفُرۡ فَلَمَّا كَفَرَ قَالَ إِنِّي بَرِيٓءࣱ مِّنكَ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
59:16.en: (And the hypocrites are) on the likeness of the devil when he telleth man to disbelieve, then, when he disbelieveth saith: Lo! I am quit of thee. Lo! I fear Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

59:17.ar: فَكَانَ عَٰقِبَتَهُمَآ أَنَّهُمَا فِي ٱلنَّارِ خَٰلِدَيۡنِ فِيهَاۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَٰٓؤُاْ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
59:17.en: And the consequence for both will be that they are in the Fire, therein abiding. Such is the reward of evil-doers

59:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ لِأَوَّلِ ٱلۡحَشۡرِۚ مَا ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْۖ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُم مَّانِعَتُهُمۡ حُصُونُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ فَأَتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَمۡ يَحۡتَسِبُواْۖ وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعۡبَۚ يُخۡرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُم بِأَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَأَيۡدِي ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ فَٱعۡتَبِرُواْ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
59:2.en: He it is Who hath caused those of the People of the Scripture who disbelieved to go forth from their homes unto the first exile. Ye deemed not that they would go forth, while they deemed that their strongholds would protect them from Allah. But Allah reached them from a place whereof they recked not, and cast terror in their hearts so that they ruined their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So learn a lesson, O ye who have eyes

59:3.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡجَلَآءَ لَعَذَّبَهُمۡ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابُ ٱلنَّارِ
59:3.en: And if Allah had not decreed migration for them, He verily would have punished them in the world, and theirs in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire

59:4.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ شَآقُّواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥۖ وَمَن يُشَآقِّ ٱللَّهَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:4.en: That is because they were opposed to Allah and His messenger; and whoso is opposed to Allah, (for him) verily Allah is stern in reprisal

59:5.ar: مَا قَطَعۡتُم مِّن لِّينَةٍ أَوۡ تَرَكۡتُمُوهَا قَآئِمَةً عَلَىٰٓ أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيُخۡزِيَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
59:5.en: Whatsoever palm-trees ye cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by Allah's leave, in order that He might confound the evil-livers

59:6.ar: وَمَآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنۡهُمۡ فَمَآ أَوۡجَفۡتُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ خَيۡلࣲ وَلَا رِكَابࣲ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُسَلِّطُ رُسُلَهُۥ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
59:6.en: And that which Allah gave as spoil unto His messenger from them, ye urged not any horse or riding-camel for the sake thereof, but Allah giveth His messenger lordship over whom He will. Allah is Able to do all things

59:7.ar: مَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ فَلِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ كَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةَۢ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡأَغۡنِيَآءِ مِنكُمۡۚ وَمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَىٰكُمۡ عَنۡهُ فَٱنتَهُواْۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:7.en: That which Allah giveth as spoil unto His messenger from the people of the townships, it is for Allah and His messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, that it become not a commodity between the rich among you. And whatsoever the messenger giveth you, take it. And whatsoever he forbiddeth, abstain (from it). And keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is stern in reprisal

59:8.ar: لِلۡفُقَرَآءِ ٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُخۡرِجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ يَبۡتَغُونَ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣰ ا وَيَنصُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصَّٰدِقُونَ
59:8.en: And (it is) for the poor fugitives who have been driven out from their homes and their belongings, who seek bounty from Allah and help Allah and His messenger. They are the loyal

59:9.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُو ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ يُحِبُّونَ مَنۡ هَاجَرَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمۡ حَاجَةࣰ مِّمَّآ أُوتُواْ وَيُؤۡثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ وَلَوۡ كَانَ بِهِمۡ خَصَاصَةࣱۚ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
59:9.en: Those who entered the city and the faith before them love those who flee unto them for refuge, and find in their breasts no need for that which hath been given them, but prefer (the fugitives) above themselves though poverty become their lot. And whoso is saved from his own avarice - such are they who are successful

59:10.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَلِإِخۡوَٰنِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِٱلۡإِيمَٰنِ وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلࣰّ ا لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ رَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
59:10.en: And those who came (into the faith) after them say: Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith, and place not in our hearts any rancour toward those who believe. Our Lord! Thou art Full of Pity, Merciful

59:11.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ نَافَقُواْ يَقُولُونَ لِإِخۡوَٰنِهِمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَئِنۡ أُخۡرِجۡتُمۡ لَنَخۡرُجَنَّ مَعَكُمۡ وَلَا نُطِيعُ فِيكُمۡ أَحَدًا أَبَدࣰ ا وَإِن قُوتِلۡتُمۡ لَنَنصُرَنَّكُمۡ وَٱللَّهُ يَشۡهَدُ إِنَّهُمۡ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
59:11.en: Hast thou not observed those who are hypocrites, (how) they tell their brethren who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture: If ye are driven out, we surely will go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, and if ye are attacked we verily will help you. And Allah beareth witness that they verily are liars

59:12.ar: لَئِنۡ أُخۡرِجُواْ لَا يَخۡرُجُونَ مَعَهُمۡ وَلَئِن قُوتِلُواْ لَا يَنصُرُونَهُمۡ وَلَئِن نَّصَرُوهُمۡ لَيُوَلُّنَّ ٱلۡأَدۡبَٰرَ ثُمَّ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
59:12.en: (For) indeed if they are driven out they go not out with them, and indeed if they are attacked they help them not, and indeed if they had helped them they would have turned and fled, and then they would not have been victorious

33:37.ar: وَإِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيٓ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡسِكۡ عَلَيۡكَ زَوۡجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخۡفِي فِي نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ وَتَخۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخۡشَىٰهُۖ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدࣱ مِّنۡهَا وَطَرࣰ ا زَوَّجۡنَٰكَهَا لِكَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجࣱ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِ أَدۡعِيَآئِهِمۡ إِذَا قَضَوۡاْ مِنۡهُنَّ وَطَرࣰ اۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا
33:37.en: And when thou saidst unto him on whom Allah hath conferred favour and thou hast conferred favour: Keep thy wife to thyself, and fear Allah. And thou didst hide in thy mind that which Allah was to bring to light, and thou didst fear mankind whereas Allah hath a better right that thou shouldst fear Him. So when Zeyd had performed that necessary formality (of divorce) from her, We gave her unto thee in marriage, so that (henceforth) there may be no sin for believers in respect of wives of their adopted sons, when the latter have performed the necessary formality (of release) from them. The commandment of Allah must be fulfilled

1:2.en: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds

14:22.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لَمَّا قُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمۡ وَعۡدَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَوَعَدتُّكُمۡ فَأَخۡلَفۡتُكُمۡۖ وَمَا كَانَ لِيَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّن سُلۡطَٰنٍ إِلَّآ أَن دَعَوۡتُكُمۡ فَٱسۡتَجَبۡتُمۡ لِيۖ فَلَا تَلُومُونِي وَلُومُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۖ مَّآ أَنَا۠ بِمُصۡرِخِكُمۡ وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُصۡرِخِيَّ إِنِّي كَفَرۡتُ بِمَآ أَشۡرَكۡتُمُونِ مِن قَبۡلُۗ إِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
14:22.en: And Satan saith, when the matter hath been decided: Lo! Allah promised you a promise of truth; and I promised you, then failed you. And I had no power over you save that I called unto you and ye obeyed me. So blame not, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can ye help me, Lo! I disbelieved in that which ye before ascribed to me. Lo! for wrong-doers is a painful doom

wzn_-nPcnrc.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Hashr, Part 5: Verses 13-17
wzn_-nPcnrc.one_line: Al-Hashr 13-17: fearing people more than Allah, hearts scattered behind a united front, Shaytan's betrayal, and division as the greatest evil.
wzn_-nPcnrc.summary: He opens with method: late Medinan surahs assume a Muslim polity, so applying them to a minority without that context breeds extremism, and tafsir needs real expertise while reflection is everyone's duty, which is why youth should learn Arabic for the Quran. Living in a country means abiding by its laws; in Medina only traitors were expelled, while hypocrites and disbelievers remained citizens. Verse 13 says the hypocrites feared the Muslims more than Allah. The Quran's critiques are mirrors, not weapons: fear no boss or government more than Allah, which takes internalised principles. The Prophet's brief fear of people's talk over marrying Zaynab was exposed at once, proving his conduct was otherwise flawless. Verse 14 describes people who look united but whose hearts are scattered and whose hostility turns inward; he insists Muslims see themselves here, unable to agree even in Ontario. A pre-Islamic poet who refused to avenge his brother rather than weaken his tribe, the Prophet who never grew angry for himself, and Uthman who gave his life to spare Muslim blood show how to take one for the team. Verses 15-17 compare division to Shaytan, who lures then disowns. Both end in the Fire, so never be a source of division over minor matters when Muslims agree on the essentials.

outline.heading: Late Medinan surahs assume a Muslim polity
outline.gist: Reading them without that context, such as applying combat verses meant for an army to a minority, is where extremism comes from.

outline.heading: Tafsir is not the same as reflection
outline.gist: Reflection on the explained meaning is every Muslim's obligation; tafsir itself requires mastery of Arabic and many disciplines.

outline.heading: Teach the youth Arabic for the sake of the Quran
outline.gist: Arabic matters only because it gives firsthand access to Allah's word; switching the khutbah to Arabic will not achieve that, investing in teaching will.

outline.heading: The surah's map of citizenship so far
outline.gist: Relations among individuals, then the groups of a country: traitors, the disadvantaged, believers old and new, hypocrites and disbelievers.

outline.heading: Abide by the laws of the country you live in
outline.gist: Traitors were evicted, not killed; a Muslim who chooses to live somewhere must respect its laws even when he disagrees with some.

outline.heading: No one but traitors was expelled
outline.gist: Hypocrites and disbelievers stayed citizens; even Banu Qurayzah's leader admitted the Prophet never punished his tribe for Banu al-Nadir's crime before he was pressured into betrayal at the Trench.

outline.heading: Recap of the hypocrites' promises and recitation
outline.gist: The hypocrites promised to leave and fight with Banu al-Nadir and lied; he recites verses 13-14.

outline.heading: They fear you more than they fear Allah
outline.gist: Rahbah here means the Muslims were a greater source of fear in their hearts than Allah.

outline.heading: Critiques in the Quran are warnings for us
outline.gist: These flaws are listed so we avoid them; a moment will come when fear of someone pulls against a clear command of Allah.

outline.heading: Belonging means fearing no one more than Allah
outline.gist: Not a boss, a government or loss of livelihood; holding firm requires principles internalised long before the test comes.

outline.heading: The Prophet, Zaynab and fear of people's talk
outline.gist: Commanded to marry Zaynab to end adoptive lineage, he briefly feared the propaganda against Islam, and the Quran exposed it.

outline.heading: One exposed lapse proves a flawless life
outline.gist: Since even this noble-minded hesitation was revealed publicly, no other lapse existed, and he conveyed it without hiding it.

outline.heading: A people who do not understand
outline.gist: Fiqh is specific understanding; fearing people more than God reflects a gap in it.

outline.heading: Fighting only from fortresses; hostility among themselves
outline.gist: They fight only from fortified towns or behind walls, and their malice toward one another is severe.

outline.heading: Be a servant, not a judge
outline.gist: Projecting the Quran onto others is a bad habit; it is meant for self-reflection.

outline.heading: You think them united but their hearts are scattered
outline.gist: The verse describes Muslims today: they march together but can't get ten people or a province's organisations to agree, and turn their harshness on each other.

outline.heading: A people who do not reason
outline.gist: Distinguishing fears takes reflection, but standing by your brethren takes no intellect at all.

outline.heading: The poet who would not avenge his brother
outline.gist: Shamed by his wife, a pre-Islamic Arab refused to take revenge on his own tribe because his arrow would strike himself; a Syrian proverb says the same.

outline.heading: Swallow your ego and take one for the team
outline.gist: If people of ignorance spared their tribe, Muslims have far more reason not to split over petty causes.

outline.heading: The Prophet never grew angry for himself
outline.gist: Taunts about him or Khadijah never provoked retaliation; he had no button to press.

outline.heading: Uthman gives his life to spare Muslim blood
outline.gist: Forewarned by the Prophet, Uthman forbade his guards to fight the rebels and was killed reciting Quran rather than let blood be spilled for him.

outline.heading: Reciting verses 15-17
outline.gist: He recites the passage and notes the dual form, which English lacks.

outline.heading: Everyone is the ummah of Muhammad
outline.gist: A prophet's ummah is everyone he was sent to, believers or not; those who responded must convey the message well to those who have not.

outline.heading: Universality versus earlier prophets
outline.gist: Musa and Isa were sent to the Children of Israel, while the Quran begins with the Lord of all the worlds and Muhammad was sent to everyone.

outline.heading: Hypocrites and disbelievers are part of the group
outline.gist: The point is not to fight or remove them; he struggles to find a historical parallel for our times.

outline.heading: Like those shortly before them
outline.gist: Division leads to confrontation and defeat, as it did for those who tasted the consequences of their choice before them.

outline.heading: Like Shaytan who lures then disowns
outline.gist: Those who push you toward division have their agenda and abandon you when it backfires.

outline.heading: Shaytan's sermon on the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: He tells his followers he only called and they answered, so they must blame themselves.

outline.heading: Both the lurer and the lured end in the Fire
outline.gist: Neither can shift the blame; division of a nation is the greatest evil, the one mistake earlier communities were told not to make.

outline.heading: Resist the urge to divide
outline.gist: When ignored or disrespected you will want to split; instead bring people together, since Muslims agree on nearly every existential question.

outline.heading: Badr: Quraysh fought their own
outline.gist: The Prophet pleaded with his own tribe and grieved over their dead; what was worth that division?

outline.heading: Outro

brnZSvwea2I.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Hashr, Part 6: Verses 18-21
brnZSvwea2I.one_line: Al-Hashr 18-21: taqwa and assessing what you send ahead, forgetting Allah and losing yourself, the only real ranking, and the humbled mountain.
brnZSvwea2I.summary: After a surah of laws for a mixed society, the ending turns spiritual because laws mean little unless people hold themselves accountable to Allah, which is what defined the early generation. Verse 18, the surah's only call to the believers, commands taqwa, which he defines from its root as prevention: before acting, ask whether this will get you in trouble now or later. Each soul must assess what it has sent ahead for both tomorrows, and since none knows when life ends, the time to start is now. Allah is Khabir, aware of why we act, so deeds done for the wrong reason count for nothing and half of religion is simply coming clean with Him. Verse 19 warns that forgetting Allah makes you forget yourself: the public mask fuses to the face, you chase mirages and lose even the joy of dua without noticing. Ask the Maker what you are for: a servant. Verse 20 replaces worldly rankings by wealth, titles or the worth assigned to people's blood with one ranking, Paradise or the Fire. Verse 21 says the Quran would humble a mountain; khashyah mixes love, respect and fear of strict justice. He urges people to reclaim time for deep reflection from their phones.

outline.heading: Laws need a spiritual ending
outline.gist: After regulating every group in the country, the surah closes sentimentally because nothing thrives on legalities alone.

outline.heading: Without self-accountability laws fail
outline.gist: If you do not feel you owe it to a power beyond you, you will find a loophole; the early Muslims obeyed because Allah was watching, not the police.

outline.heading: Meccan-sounding verses inside Medinan surahs
outline.gist: Every second surah of this juz has moving verses on Allah's majesty to balance the technical rulings.

outline.heading: Never forget why you do it all
outline.gist: You can get lost in an ocean of dos and don'ts; the point is the love of Allah. He recites verse 18.

outline.heading: The surah's only call to the believers
outline.gist: 'O you who believe' marks Medinan revelation; after all the social rules the command is not political but taqwa.

outline.heading: Taqwa as prevention
outline.gist: From the root of protecting and preventing: think ahead so you are not held accountable in a way you dislike, and treat people well because Allah asked, not only because the law says.

outline.heading: Assess what you sent ahead for tomorrow
outline.gist: The lam turns the verb into a command; tomorrow means both the next few decades and the life after, and every deed is a deposit.

outline.heading: Taqwa's simple question
outline.gist: The only verse with taqwa twice: ask 'will this get me in trouble?', a lower bar than 'will this please Allah?', which permits the whole permissible category.

outline.heading: If tonight were your last
outline.gist: Most people do not know their last breath is coming; there is no age to start preparing, only now.

outline.heading: Al-Khabir knows the inside of deeds
outline.gist: Among the names of knowledge, Khabir is awareness of intentions and feelings, because what matters in a deed is why it is done.

outline.heading: Deeds for the wrong reason count for nothing
outline.gist: Following rules out of fear of the law or habit earns nothing; we are an open book to Allah however we manage our public face.

outline.heading: Half of religion is coming clean with Allah
outline.gist: Admit to Him that you take credit you do not deserve and ask for mercy from that honest position; it is a release.

outline.heading: People assume, Allah knows
outline.gist: Others can see what you do and guess why, which is itself a sin; Allah knows the reason.

outline.heading: Forgetting Allah makes you forget yourself
outline.gist: The worldly punishment is not that Allah neglects you but that you lose who you are and what you are for.

outline.heading: Chasing mirages
outline.gist: You reach the goals you dreamed of and remain as miserable, so you chase the next thing, and nothing leads to nothing.

outline.heading: The mask fused to the face
outline.gist: Everyone needs a public persona, but forgetting Allah lets it become you until you believe it.

outline.heading: Allah knows you and loves your potential
outline.gist: He knew you before your genetic code existed and still loves what you can become.

outline.heading: Before Allah you stand bare
outline.gist: No titles or signature; you come alone as you were first created, leaving your accounts and followers behind.

outline.heading: The worshipper who lost the joy of dua
outline.gist: A man who saw no punishment for years of sin was told in a dream that losing the sweetness of supplication was his punishment.

outline.heading: Not knowing yourself, you do not know what you need
outline.gist: You are fooled into needing wealth and fame; those who know Allah would give up anything but that closeness.

outline.heading: The remorse of the blessing never picked up
outline.gist: Imagine watching your life story with the greatest gift in front of you the whole time while you looked past it.

outline.heading: Fasiq in the Quran and in fiqh
outline.gist: In the Quran it means deviating after having the chance, not a curse word; terms like sunnah have different definitions in each discipline.

outline.heading: Neglecting Allah for later starves the spirit
outline.gist: Setting Allah aside until after school or work leaves the spirit unfed; it survives years of deprivation waiting to be nourished.

outline.heading: Ask the Maker what you are for
outline.gist: The manufacturer defines the purpose: you are a servant of One who needs nothing from you, and embracing that changes your ambitions.

outline.heading: The people of Fire and Paradise are not equal
outline.gist: The world ranks people by wealth, lineage, colour and power, even valuing some people's blood above thousands of others; these rankings are phony.

outline.heading: The only ranking: good deeds versus sins
outline.gist: Titles and family are stripped away; you stand with your name and your deeds, and only those who always ranked themselves this way are not shocked.

outline.heading: Already aware of your real standing
outline.gist: Someone who knows his good deeds are thin is busy making up ground rather than being fooled by illusions; he then recites verse 21.

outline.heading: Had this Quran come down on a mountain
outline.gist: A mountain seems lifeless and harsh, as mountain people are compared with valley people, yet it would be humbled.

outline.heading: Humbled and split apart; hearts harder than rock
outline.gist: Khashi' is submission of the mind as well as the heart; some rocks split for water while some hearts stay harder.

outline.heading: Khashyah: love, respect and fear of justice
outline.gist: In this world we fear injustice; before Allah we fear being treated with strict fairness and hope for His bounty instead.

outline.heading: These are similes so people reflect
outline.gist: The prophets contemplated, as Muhammad did in Hira; phones have destroyed the space for deep thought that weighs scenarios and arguments.

outline.heading: Why the Quran does not move us
outline.gist: We forgot Allah, so He took back the ability to know what is valuable.

outline.heading: Outro

b4BOoDoB9hQ.speaker_note: single voice; recalls growing up in Syria and his dawah work at this masjid
b4BOoDoB9hQ.title: Assessment of the Current Events and What We Can Do
b4BOoDoB9hQ.one_line: Reading Al-Buruj, he warns that those who merely watch oppression are accountable, then answers how to cope, why the world disagrees, and what to do.
b4BOoDoB9hQ.summary: He recites Al-Buruj and argues that the people of the trench condemned in it are not only the tyrants who burned the believers but the onlookers who sat back and watched; the repeated language of witnessing makes inaction a choice we will answer for, like an older sibling blamed for not stopping a younger one. Turning to Gaza two weeks into the bombing, he describes professionals fired for solidarity, support for Palestinians branded as antisemitism, and a double standard over who bombed a hospital, calling it intellectual oppression no different from the Syria he left. He then answers three questions. To cope, find others in the masjid who feel the same. The world believes otherwise because of the narrative people absorb from childhood and because media always carries the storyteller's bias. What to do: protests, emails and petitions are needed but short-term, fading when the bombing stops. Real change needs lifelong commitment, which he calls the hardest part of his own work: learning the deen, raising children, professional success, strong families and unity. He ends with the Prophet telling Abu Talib he could no more stop than light a candle from the sun.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Buruj: the oaths and the people of the trench
outline.gist: Allah swears by the sky, the promised day and every witness, then curses the people of the trench; believers who changed their faith under a tyrant were burned in a trench before the Prophet was born.

outline.heading: Sitting back, not sitting on the fire
outline.gist: The common reading that the victims sat on the fire is linguistically impossible; the word means sitting back from what you should have done, so the condemned here are not the tyrants, whose guilt needs no verse.

outline.heading: The third group: those who only watched
outline.gist: Besides the perpetrators and the victims there is a group that just witnessed; the root of witnessing appears four times in six verses, and the believers were persecuted only for believing in the One who witnesses everything.

outline.heading: "I didn't do anything": the older sibling
outline.gist: On Judgment Day that answer is exactly the charge, like the older child blamed for what a younger sibling broke; not doing anything is also a choice we are held to.

outline.heading: Silenced for solidarity, as in Syria
outline.gist: Professionals fired and support for Palestinians labelled antisemitic or pro-terror; he left Syria for freedom of speech and finds it missing here when it matters, since taking a livelihood is worse than beheading.

outline.heading: The hospital bombing and intellectual oppression
outline.gist: One side gets a years-long investigation, the other is presumed evil; forcing one narrative on people is political tyranny wherever it happens.

outline.heading: We are all Palestinian
outline.gist: Everyone here descends from or supports the families of the Holy Land, so we stand by them and their right to be free and treated as human.

outline.heading: Question one: how to cope
outline.gist: With thousands killed and injured, you are not alone; calamities are when people in the masjid must find each other and reach out to those struggling like them.

outline.heading: The issue itself is simple
outline.gist: A land promised by one foreign group to another, its people ethnically cleansed over decades, and illegal settlements still being built against the UN.

outline.heading: Question two: the narrative people grow up with
outline.gist: Ask why others believe otherwise; people here are fed a narrative from early childhood about a region they barely know, and most of us support whatever those around us support.

outline.heading: No story is told without bias
outline.gist: Media is not a neutral source of truth; those who control the storytelling push what they believe, so the slant should not surprise us.

outline.heading: Interlude
Question three: short-term actions are not enough
outline.gist: Protests, emails and petitions are needed during the calamity but fade once the bombing stops; what changes things is the long haul, which is boring, tiring and makes no headlines.

outline.heading: The hardest part of dawah: commitment
outline.gist: Asked by a brother what is most difficult in his work, he answered commitment: people float in for a few months and disappear for years.

outline.heading: Without lasting commitment the cycle repeats
outline.gist: Activism must never die off, and Muslims of every culture must unite and stand by each other; otherwise each cycle of atrocity wears us down a little more.

outline.heading: A lifetime of work
outline.gist: Learning the deen, educating children, supporting the community, succeeding academically and professionally and building strong families is how we answer; it is meant to be a lifetime of work.

outline.heading: Waiting for others is weakness
outline.gist: Relying on others to stop the killing because we lack unity, voice and leverage is helplessness, yet we lack neither numbers, expertise, wealth, youth nor conviction.

outline.heading: Abu Talib and the Prophet's resolve
outline.gist: Only commitment is missing; asked through Abu Talib to tone it down, the Prophet said he could no more stop than they could light a candle from the sun, and Abu Talib pledged to support him.

outline.heading: Outro

5:8.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۖ وَلَا يَجۡرِمَنَّكُمۡ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوۡمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعۡدِلُواْۚ ٱعۡدِلُواْ هُوَ أَقۡرَبُ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
5:8.en: O ye who believe! Be steadfast witnesses for Allah in equity, and let not hatred of any people seduce you that ye deal not justly. Deal justly, that is nearer to your duty. Observe your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Informed of what ye do

5:2.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُحِلُّواْ شَعَٰٓئِرَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا ٱلشَّهۡرَ ٱلۡحَرَامَ وَلَا ٱلۡهَدۡيَ وَلَا ٱلۡقَلَٰٓئِدَ وَلَآ ءَآمِّينَ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ ٱلۡحَرَامَ يَبۡتَغُونَ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣰ اۚ وَإِذَا حَلَلۡتُمۡ فَٱصۡطَادُواْۚ وَلَا يَجۡرِمَنَّكُمۡ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوۡمٍ أَن صَدُّوكُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ أَن تَعۡتَدُواْۘ وَتَعَاوَنُواْ عَلَى ٱلۡبِرِّ وَٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُواْ عَلَى ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٰنِۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
5:2.en: O ye who believe! Profane not Allah's monuments nor the Sacred Month nor the offerings nor the garlands, nor those repairing to the Sacred House, seeking the grace and pleasure of their Lord. But when ye have left the sacred territory, then go hunting (if ye will). And let not your hatred of a folk who (once) stopped your going to the inviolable place of worship seduce you to transgress; but help ye one another unto righteousness and pious duty. Help not one another unto sin and transgression, but keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is severe in punishment

OggrP-7EBFQ.speaker_note: single voice; speaks of being a third generation Canadian who was expelled from another country, addresses his masjid in London
OggrP-7EBFQ.title: Five Points to Consider During Difficult Times
OggrP-7EBFQ.one_line: During the October 2023 bombing of Gaza, five instructions: keep advocating, never lose hope, keep your ethics, unite, and comfort each other.
OggrP-7EBFQ.summary: He admits he has come to dread Friday because he has no words for what is happening in Gaza, and says that for the second time in his life he feels unheard and unsafe in his own country, asking how a democracy can blacklist citizens for an opinion. He then offers five points. First, advocacy must continue in whatever lane each person is good at, for the rest of their lives, because the world counts on short attention spans; every individual voice matters. Second, despair is not permitted for a believer: he draws on the Prophet extracting hope from the boulder at the Trench and from comforting his daughter after a man threw sand in his face, and reads the harsh verse of Al-Hajj about those who think Allah will not grant victory. Victory may come after our lifetime, and that should be acceptable. Third, never compromise ethics or justice because others have transgressed, citing the verses on being barred from the Haram. In the second khutbah he asks the community to drop grudges and unite, since strength is in unity rather than numbers, and to reach out to anyone who feels isolated or scared. He closes on the firing of the Western University chaplain and refusing to be bullied.

outline.heading: Opening
Dreading Jumuah
outline.gist: He has never before wished Friday farther away; his words are failing him, and as a third-generation Canadian he does not feel he belongs to his own country.

outline.heading: Unheard and unsafe in his own country
outline.gist: The second time in his life he has felt this, after being expelled from his first country; citizens blacklisted for an opinion is no democracy, and a third-world tyranny was at least honest about it.

outline.heading: Point one: keep advocating in your own lane
outline.gist: Nobody knows the single right way, so do whatever form of advocacy you are good at within the framework of the country.

outline.heading: Carpet bombing on live news
outline.gist: Never before has carpet bombing of a dense population been watched live: a reporter told on air his family is dead, a two-year-old in shock; how does that not enter anyone's decisions?

outline.heading: The world banks on short attention spans
outline.gist: Email politicians and people of influence, write, protest, post, lobby; the world counts on people getting bored in two weeks.

outline.heading: A hill to die on: every voice matters
outline.gist: From two billion Muslims down to this city, this masjid and then you; never belittle your voice or any good deed, even a smile.

outline.heading: Advocacy for life: a turning point
outline.gist: Our generation will not be forgiven if it returns to normal; never have so many lost their jobs, the youth have built a backbone, and better organization can change the country's political norm.

outline.heading: Point two: despair is not permitted
outline.gist: Only the disbelievers and the misguided lose hope in their Lord's mercy; pulling hope out of the darkest moments was a hallmark of the Prophet.

outline.heading: The boulder at the Trench
outline.gist: Starving and frightened, the diggers could not break a boulder; with three strikes the Prophet promised Persia, Yemen and Rome, and the same people later saw those treasures brought to Madinah.

outline.heading: Projecting hope through action
outline.gist: The best person is the one who projects the most hope, not by words but by showing others you still stand for what is right and never stop.

outline.heading: The Prophet and his weeping daughter
outline.gist: When a man threw sand in his face, he told his daughter, likely Zaynab, not to cry because Allah would grant her father success; this was confidence, not prophecy.

outline.heading: Al-Hajj: whoever thinks Allah will not give victory
outline.gist: The harsh verse tells such a person to stretch a rope and see if it helps; success may come after our lifetime, because it is about righteousness prevailing, not about us.

outline.heading: Point three: do not stoop to their level
outline.gist: Those in the mud want you down with them so that everyone looks equally corrupt; never compromise your ethics, values or principles.

outline.heading: Barred from the Haram, still not to transgress
outline.gist: Hatred of a people must not make you unjust; Quraysh broke Arabia's one universal law by turning the Muslims away from the Haram, and Allah still told them not to let that make them transgressors.

outline.heading: Interlude
Point four: pull together
outline.gist: Drop grudges in hard times; unity is an obligation and strength lies in togetherness, not numbers, unlike the foam on the ocean; quarrelling while a family is in pain is shameful.

outline.heading: Point five: reach out and comfort
outline.gist: Feeling isolated, scared and targeted is human; walk the dark tunnel holding someone's hand toward the light, and look after yourself too.

outline.heading: Closing: refuse to be bullied
outline.gist: The Western University chaplain was fired, leaving students without their one supporter; we ask only to be heard equally, and history is recording how we behave.

outline.heading: Outro
